premises.text: Existing recommendation systems rely on stranger reviews, non-personalized averages, and widespread fake reviews
premises.evidence_span: all of these systems are dependent on giving you reviews and recommendations from strangers

premises.text: LiveStar surfaces recommendations from professional critics and from friends the user knows whom to trust
premises.evidence_span: give you access to high-quality reviews from trusted sources

premises.text: An algorithm finds people with matching taste and exposes their recommendations
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar algorithmically measures your taste and then compares it to other people

premises.text: Q&A via email, SMS, and Facebook with pre-populated surveys makes friend recommendations easy
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar has a Q&A feature that lets me send a question, a request for some recommendations to friends who have never heard of LiveStar via email, SMS, and Facebook

premises.text: One app covers restaurants, menu items, music, and movies as a multi-category destination
premises.evidence_span: you can go to LiveStar for restaurants, what to eat when you're at the restaurant, what music to listen to, and what movie to watch

value.text: Fast, high-quality personalized recommendations from trusted sources
value.evidence_span: provides fast access to high quality sources across a range of common real world scenarios

notes: Three critique points folded into one broken-status-quo premise. Critics/friends/similar-taste are uses of one trusted-source mechanism plus algorithmic matching and Q&A as enabling features; similar-taste kept as own premise because speaker claims uniqueness. Singleton D3: multi-category scope presented as separate destination claim.
